# OpenAI 大模型算法岗系统训练工程

This is an open-source book series for interview preparation and capability building for large model algorithm roles.

It is not a collection of scattered notes but a complete training system. It covers machine learning fundamentals, Transformer, LLM training, alignment, inference deployment, inference frameworks, AI Infra, evaluation and safety, paper close reading, project practice, system design, the tool protocol ecosystem, and mock interviews. Step by step, it helps readers build the theory, engineering, research, and communication skills that large model algorithm roles require.

The purpose of this book series is not to list knowledge points but to help readers build a transferable knowledge map of large models. For important concepts, it tries to explain the historical background, the motivation for the idea, the problems with earlier methods, the characteristics of current methods, their strengths and weaknesses, their applicable boundaries, the directions later work has improved on, and how they relate to adjacent concepts. The project is beginner-friendly by default but targets readers at every stage: beginners can follow the context and background, intermediate readers can connect the systems framework, and advanced readers can see mechanism details, engineering trade-offs, and interview deep-dive points.

Suitable readers:

1. Students who want to prepare systematically for large model algorithm interviews.
2. Engineers moving into the LLM field from traditional algorithm engineering, backend engineering, or data science.
3. Learners who want to fill gaps in LLM principles, training, alignment, inference, evaluation, and the engineering deployment system.
4. Beginners who want to build a global view of large model research and engineering and gradually form a project portfolio.

## 维护记录与研究资料

All architecture reviews of the books, chapter reviews, revisions to the main text or supporting materials, revision decisions, completion status, outstanding issues, and follow-up handoffs are uniformly and exclusively recorded in [`progress/`](https://github.com/ChanChiChoi/llm-from-zero-to-interview/blob/HEAD/progress/). Book progress and revision history must not be written into `research/`, `plan.md`, `README.md`, or the main text.

[`research/`](https://github.com/ChanChiChoi/llm-from-zero-to-interview/blob/HEAD/research/) only records new knowledge points discovered through web search, along with their source evidence, including sources, versions or dates, evidence scope, and unverified boundaries. It does not record per-book or per-chapter refinement progress, revision history, or audit logs. The project plan and the long-term writing standards master outline are at [`plan.md`](https://github.com/ChanChiChoi/llm-from-zero-to-interview/blob/HEAD/plan.md) and [`写作规范/总纲.md`](https://github.com/ChanChiChoi/llm-from-zero-to-interview/blob/HEAD/写作规范/总纲.md), respectively.

Li-ong-o/macOSHello.body:
# macOSHello

macOSHello is a purely local face unlock tool for the macOS menu bar. It uses the built-in Vision framework for face detection and feature recognition, and AVFoundation to capture camera frames. All recognition runs on the local machine. It does not require a network connection, and it does not upload camera frames or face features.

## Features

- Multi-face enrollment, with 8 sets of local feature samples saved for each face
- Face recognition, similarity threshold judgment, and real-time similarity display
- Basic liveness detection, which requires slowly turning the head during enrollment and recognition
- Enumerate and select a built-in or external camera
- Recognize the two most relevant faces in the frame and select the one with the highest similarity for matching
- Automatically recognize after the lock screen, screen wake, system wake, or screen saver appears
- After locking, a cooldown of 20 or 60 seconds can be set to avoid being unlocked automatically before the person has left
- When no one is present, check at a low frequency. When someone is present but not matched, increase the retry interval. It does not permanently stop after a fixed number of failures
- The password is stored in the local keychain. After successful recognition, the currently logged-in session is unlocked
- Stops face detection when the display is off or the system sleeps, to avoid keeping the camera occupied for long periods
- Supports setting launch at login

## How It Works

### Face Enrollment

During enrollment, macOSHello reads camera frames through AVFoundation, then uses Vision to perform the following processing:

1. `VNDetectFaceRectanglesRequest` detects face regions in the frame.
2. `VNDetectFaceCaptureQualityRequest` evaluates face quality. Low-quality frames are discarded.
3. `VNGenerateImageFeaturePrintRequest` generates the face feature vector.
4. Saves 8 feature vectors that meet the pose variation requirements to `~/.macOSHello/faces.json`. New archives use `embeddingVersion 2`.

During enrollment, the range of yaw and pitch changes is recorded, and slow head turns are required. This is not 3D structured-light liveness detection like Face ID. It is basic pose variation detection.

### Face Recognition

During recognition, the same Vision requests generate the current face feature vector, which is then compared with the enrolled samples using cosine similarity:

```text
current feature vector · enrolled sample vector / (length of current vector × length of enrolled sample)
```

Each frame produces a similarity score. Recognition succeeds only when all of the following conditions are met:

- The current frame's similarity reaches the configured threshold, for example `0.83`
- 8 consecutive frames all reach the threshold
- When basic liveness detection is enabled, the pose variation range meets the requirements

Therefore, "the highest similarity exceeds the threshold" does not by itself mean recognition succeeded. If any frame falls below the threshold midway, the consecutive count restarts.

Recognition calculates similarity separately for the first two faces detected by Vision and uses the best candidate. Archives from older versions do not have the `embeddingVersion` marker. During recognition, both the old and new feature formats are supported. After upgrading, re-enrolling faces is recommended for more stable recognition results.

# Miaoxiang Stock Screening · Intraday Cumulative Watchlist

Use Eastmoney's "Miaoxiang" stock screener to **continuously add qualifying A-shares to the same watchlist during trading hours**, deduplicated by stock code. When the same stock is hit multiple times, its "selection count" is incremented and the scan timestamp of each hit is recorded, making it easier to review the stock's intraday movement pattern.

## Current screening criteria (A-shares)
- Excluded: Beijing Stock Exchange / STAR Market (688) / ChiNext (300) / ST stocks / delisted stocks
- Excluded risk events: risk of new-rule price-cap designation, share reduction plans within the past three months, lock-up expirations within the next three months, regulatory letters or regulatory work letters within the past three months
- Price-volume and technicals: price change of 3%–5%, volume ratio > 1.5, turnover rate of 5%–10%, total market capitalization of CNY 5–20 billion (50–200 亿), and a limit-up within the past 20 trading days
- Fundamentals: excludes stocks whose latest reporting period net profit is negative, and stocks with a debt-to-asset ratio above 70%

> In addition to the conditions in the Miaoxiang QUERY, the script performs a **secondary hard fundamentals check** on candidates at the code level (Eastmoney F10 financial interface): TTM net profit attributable to shareholders < 0 or debt-to-asset ratio > 70% blocks the stock directly, without relying on the AI interface to follow the prompt.

> To change the conditions: edit the single `QUERY` at the top of `screener_monitor.py`. Both monitoring and scheduled tasks will follow.

## Cloud auto-run (primary, no local machine required)
The repository has GitHub Actions configured (`.github/workflows/monitor.yml`), which **automatically wakes up every 5 minutes during trading hours**. Each run internally uses **`--loop` mode to scan about every 2 minutes** (3 times per run by default), raising the effective screening frequency to about every 2 minutes:

- Each cloud run = one `git pull` (fetch the latest pool) → loop scanning (every 2 minutes, automatically guarded by trading hours) → a single `git commit + push` at the end, avoiding frequent git conflicts.

Knowledge is a wealth jointly created by humanity, and videos that explain knowledge should be as free as free software. Each film is released together with its complete source code, giving users four freedoms:

|---|---|
| Run | Anyone can watch, screen, and use these videos for any purpose |
| Study | Every frame is f(t), every line of narration has a source, and every number can be recalculated from the experiment |

**Content over form.** Reliable facts, clear explanation, and coherent narrative matter more than complex form. Visuals, sound, and technology serve understanding, and good documentation lets the next participant read, look up, and continue the work.

**Open source is part of delivery.** Whether self-made, commissioned from third parties, or produced through external collaboration, each work must deliver editable source code, production steps, and corresponding licenses. leizongmin/ZeroWeb.body:
# ZeroWeb

ZeroWeb is an experimental cross-platform browser written in Rust from scratch, supporting macOS, Linux, Windows, and Android. It delivers two things:

- **`ZeroWebView`**: a web rendering library that can be embedded in other applications
- **`ZeroBrowser`**: a full browser application built on the same engine

DOM, CSS, layout, rendering, JavaScript bindings, networking, and security boundaries are all implemented in this repository, mainly relying on Rust components under permissive licenses.

This is also an AI-first engineering experiment: humans are responsible only for solution design, key decisions, and result verification, while nearly all of the code is written by AI. We want to see how far AI can advance a complex system like a browser when architectural boundaries, tests, and acceptance criteria are clearly defined.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The project is experimental and **is not a browser for everyday use**. It is suitable for learning, research, and engineering exploration. For commercial or production use, please evaluate the feature, security, compatibility, performance, and licensing risks yourself.

## Why this project

- **Embedding first**: In addition to the browser application, it provides a stable Rust `ZeroWebView` API for direct integration into other applications.
- **Clear licensing boundaries**: Mainline dependencies prefer permissive licenses such as MIT, Apache-2.0, and BSD, so core capabilities are not subject to copyleft constraints.
- **Full-stack Rust**: The page engine, host layer, and rendering infrastructure are built within the Rust ecosystem wherever possible.
- **AI can write, but must be reviewable**: Every change must be clearly explained, testable, and visible.

## Current progress

Status legend: ✅ basic capability available with test coverage; 🚧 in progress and not yet complete; ⏳ planned.

# Hysteria 2 One-Click Deployment and Management Script

**Hysteria 2** one-click deployment script for the official server, with a built-in Web console, multi-user management, and cluster integration, optimized for high packet loss and UDP QoS environments.

## ✨ Features

- **Hysteria 2 main protocol**: official binaries (amd64 / arm64 / armv7), port hopping enabled by default (UDP 20000-40000) and Salamander obfuscation; certificates support self-signed, existing certificates, or automatic Let's Encrypt issuance for a domain.
- **Backup channels (optional, one-click start/stop via web)**:
  - **VLESS-Reality** (TCP): borrows certificates from major vendors for the handshake, no domain required;
  - **VMess-WS-TLS**, **VLESS Encryption** (post-quantum key exchange), **AnyTLS**: require a domain and a trusted certificate;
  - **TUIC v5** (QUIC / UDP, carried by sing-box): requires a domain and a trusted certificate; the port is automatically selected from 41000-49999 (avoiding the port hopping range); cloud security groups must allow this UDP port.
  - Delivered in subscriptions alongside Hy2; Clash / sing-box use url-test to automatically pick the best option; when UDP is throttled, traffic automatically falls back to TCP.
  - ⚠️ **AnyTLS traffic is not currently counted toward users' used traffic, nor does it occupy "simultaneously online IP" slots**: it runs in a separate sing-box process, and the upstream Clash API does not expose per-user usage. Disabling, expiry, or exceeding quota still revokes its login credentials, but AnyTLS alone cannot trigger quota limits. For billing-sensitive users, prefer the Hy2 or Xray protocols.

- **Extension services**: GOST inbound proxy (SOCKS5 / HTTP / HTTPS), Cloudflare WARP split routing (AI sites use a clean egress), AmneziaWG anti-DPI VPN.
- **Multi-user**: each user has an independent expiry time, traffic quota, and simultaneous online IP limit, metered by real traffic; disabling, expiry, exceeding quota, or deletion takes effect immediately across all protocols and disconnects existing connections.
- **Cluster nodes**: built-in REST API, can integrate with the Teyir console or card-sales storefronts, and supports whole-machine disable and restore on traffic overage.
